title: Advanced Geometry — Circles and Polygons
tagline: Year 3 — Chords, tangents, angle properties of circles, and interior angles and diagonals of polygons

introduction.overview: Year 2 covered triangles and basic mensuration. Year 3 focuses on the circle theorems and polygon properties that appear most often in aptitude tests: the angle at the centre and at the circumference, tangent lengths, chords and the perpendicular from the centre, cyclic quadrilaterals, and the angle sum and diagonal count of regular polygons.
introduction.placementRelevance: Geometry questions in company tests are short, formula-driven problems such as tangent lengths, chord distances and polygon angles.
introduction.realWorldContext: Gear design, circular tracks, architecture and map-making use circle and polygon properties.

learningObjectives: Use the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
Apply the tangent-length and chord-distance relations
Find interior and exterior angles of regular polygons
Count diagonals of an n-sided polygon

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: The sum of angles of a triangle is 180°. Pythagoras: a² + b² = c². Area of a circle πr², circumference 2πr.

coreDefinitions: Chord: a segment joining two points of a circle. The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.
Tangent: a line touching the circle at one point; it is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
Cyclic quadrilateral: all four vertices lie on a circle; opposite angles add up to 180°.
Regular polygon: all sides and all angles are equal.
Exterior angles of any convex polygon add up to 360°.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Circles are about symmetry around the centre. Draw the radius to every point of contact or chord end; the right triangles that appear give lengths through Pythagoras.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Draw the radius and the perpendicular from the centre. Most chord and tangent questions reduce to a right triangle.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Centre angle
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference

mainNarrative: The angle that an arc subtends at the centre is twice the angle it subtends at any point on the remaining circumference. If an arc subtends 40° at the circumference, it subtends 80° at the centre.

The tangent from an external point P at distance d from the centre of a circle of radius r has length √(d² − r²). For d = 13 and r = 5 the tangent length is 12. Two tangents from the same point are equal.
A chord of length 16 in a circle of radius 10 is at distance √(10² − 8²) = 6 from the centre, because the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.
In a cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles add up to 180°. If one angle is 70° the opposite angle is 110°. The exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.
A regular polygon with n sides has each interior angle (n − 2) × 180°/n and each exterior angle 360°/n. A hexagon has interior angle 120°, exterior angle 60° and 6 × 3/2 = 9 diagonals.

deepDiveAspects.title: Angle in a semicircle
deepDiveAspects.content: It is always 90°, because the angle at the centre is 180°.

deepDiveAspects.title: Equal chords
deepDiveAspects.content: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre and subtend equal angles at the centre.

solvedExamples.title: Tangent length
solvedExamples.question: A point P is 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. Find the length of the tangent from P.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Right triangle at the point of contact.

steps.title: Triangle
steps.explanation: Radius is perpendicular to the tangent.

solvedExamples.title: Chord distance
solvedExamples.question: A chord of length 16 cm is in a circle of radius 10 cm. Find its distance from the centre.

solvedExamples.title: Regular polygon
solvedExamples.question: Find the number of sides of a regular polygon whose each interior angle is 150°.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Join centre to the chord end or tangent point; the right triangle gives the answer by Pythagoras.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the full chord in Pythagoras

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Tangent length must be shorter than the distance to the centre.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Draw the figure with all radii first.
